nodes.label: Async fill delivery mirrors exchange WS
nodes.rationale: placeOrder returns immediate ack/reject like a REST response; fills/cancels arrive asynchronously as OrderEvents via onEvent, mirroring real exchange WS delivery.
nodes.norm_label: async fill delivery mirrors exchange ws

nodes.label: Explicit validated transitions are sole truth
nodes.rationale: Any transition not in the table is a bug and is rejected; single source of truth for what can happen next to an order. CANCEL_PENDING may still fill before cancel lands.
nodes.norm_label: explicit validated transitions are sole truth

nodes.label: Crash recovery rebuilds from exchange truth
nodes.rationale: On restart never trust local store alone; rebuild each live order's state from exchange truth. A timed-out submit that actually landed is adopted, not lost or double-sent. SUBMITTED orders not yet visible (REST lag) are left, not cancelled.
nodes.norm_label: crash recovery rebuilds from exchange truth

nodes.label: Real fills come from reconciler not adapter
nodes.rationale: Real adapters emit ORDER_OPENED/ORDER_REJECTED only; fills are NOT emitted here. Real fills are detected by the execution-sync loop (OrderReconciler against exchange truth), like an exchange delivering fills asynchronously.
nodes.norm_label: real fills come from reconciler not adapter

nodes.label: Fill dedup by fillId; exchange truth wins
nodes.rationale: All state changes go through the validated state machine, no ad-hoc mutation. Fills deduped by fillId so re-delivery/replay never double-counts. setReconciled sets absolute filled qty/status directly rather than replaying events (which would double-count) because exchange truth wins.
nodes.norm_label: fill dedup by fillid; exchange truth wins

nodes.label: Pure deterministic drift detection
nodes.rationale: Compares exchange truth against local view emitting classified DriftIssues. No I/O, side effects, or dispatch. Severity: GHOST_ORDER/DUPLICATE_FILL/NEGATIVE_INVENTORY/IMPOSSIBLE_BALANCE=CRITICAL; BALANCE_MISMATCH/MISSING_FILL/STALE_LOCAL_ORDER=HARD; TIMING_LAG=SOFT.

nodes.label: Exchange truth wins; fills appended never overwritten
nodes.rationale: Financial consensus loop: fetch truth, read local view, detect+classify, repair (exchange wins for balances/orders via full replace, fills appended+deduped never overwritten), persist report. Repair skipped on CRITICAL. CRITICAL sets requiresExecutionHalt; DB is durability/audit not truth authority.
nodes.norm_label: exchange truth wins; fills appended never overwritten

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM authenticated credential encryption
nodes.rationale: Encrypts user exchange credentials at rest using master ENCRYPTION_KEY. GCM auth tag detects tampering. Without a 64-hex key, an ephemeral key is used and stored credentials will not survive restart (dev only).

nodes.label: Only place credentials are read
nodes.rationale: The only place in the system that reads credentials from a TradingSession. Credentials captured at construction, held only by the client instance scoped to session lifetime; factory keeps no reference. WS clients are public, no credentials.

nodes.norm_label: authenticated client exposes rest clients, never raw keys

nodes.label: Chaos-first classification rule
nodes.rationale: Unhealthy exchange, unhealthy reconciliation, blown spread or liquidity collapse short-circuit to CHAOTIC before any ATR/return math runs. Health degradation is treated as indistinguishable from extreme volatility so the system defaults to the most restrictive regime rather than trusting stale numbers. PAPER_MODE is explicitly exempted from the reconciliation requirement so paper runs are not permanently CHAOTIC.

nodes.label: Min-of-caps sizing model
nodes.rationale: Every constraint (reserve floor, liquidity participation, daily limits, USDT affordability, mode multiplier, volatility multiplier) is expressed as an independent cap on quantity and the binding one is simply the minimum. This makes new risk rules additive rather than nested conditionals, and every binding cap name is returned in reasons so a REDUCE/REJECT is always explainable. READ_ONLY/HALT multiply to 0, which converts mode enforcement into the same cap arithmetic.

nodes.label: Paper orders never persisted
nodes.rationale: Paper orders are simulation artifacts, so save() no-ops on order.paper and loadActive() hardcodes paper:false. Only non-terminal real orders are reloaded on boot, so idempotency and crash recovery survive restart without simulation contaminating durable truth. Missing-table (P2021) degrades to an empty in-memory registry rather than failing boot.

nodes.label: Event-parity paper simulation
nodes.rationale: PaperEngine emits the EXACT same OrderEvent shapes as a real adapter so the registry and treasury cannot tell the difference; this is what lets real Phase 5 rules run unmodified over virtual money. Realism knobs (slippageBps, fillProbability, injectable rng) make paper PnL pessimistic and tests deterministic; slippage is always adverse on both sides.

nodes.label: Staged execution gate (MODE/RISK/IDEMPOTENCY/ADAPTER)
nodes.rationale: Risk is evaluated before any order exists; HALT escalates via onRiskHalt, REDUCE rewrites quantity, and clientOrderId is derived deterministically from requestId so duplicates are caught by both an in-process set and the registry. Adapter choice is decided purely by state.mode === PAPER_MODE, and a missing real adapter is a refusal rather than a silent paper fallback. A thrown placeOrder marks the order FAILED and logs that it may still exist on the exchange.

nodes.label: Settings frozen while a soak runs
nodes.rationale: /soak_set is refused while a soak is live so a run's parameters are internally consistent end-to-end and its run record is comparable. Starting flips the engine to PAPER_MODE and stopping returns it to READ_ONLY; the driver re-checks mode every tick as a second, independent guard. RESERVE_FLOOR is deliberately NOT settable here — it comes from cfg so it can never desync from the RiskEngine that enforces it.
nodes.norm_label: settings frozen while a soak runs

nodes.label: Intent-anchored sell bucket occupancy
nodes.rationale: Occupancy is keyed on the submitted bid (sellIntentPrice), not the slipped fill price. Gating on the bid while recording the slipped fill let a 12bps slip straddle a 15bps bucket boundary and free the zone immediately — 255 sells across ~19 buckets on Jun-11. Buckets are geometric (log-based) so a band is regime-independent and history-free, and occupancy frees automatically when the cycle COMPLETES, which fixes the lastSellPrice trap where a rebought zone stayed permanently locked.

nodes.label: FIFO rebuy matching without price re-gating
nodes.rationale: onBuy does NOT re-filter by price: the driver already gated on openCyclesForRebuy(ask), so re-checking the fill price double-jeopardies the decision. With buy-side slippage the fill lands just above target on a shallow dip, the re-gate returns empty, and bought ZIG recovers nothing — cycles strand with rebought>0 and done=0 (the June-10 bug). FIFO over all open cycles pays the oldest obligation first; honesty is preserved because harvestedUsdt = grossSell - spentRebuy - fees regardless of which cycle absorbed the buy.
nodes.norm_label: fifo rebuy matching without price re-gating

nodes.label: Completed cycles, not realized PnL, as the success metric
nodes.rationale: Raw realized PnL cannot answer 'did it actually harvest?' — a sell alone books PnL without completing a round trip. Cycles make the question answerable: harvestedUsdt counts COMPLETED cycles only, outstandingSellUsdt and unrecoveredZig expose proceeds and inventory still in flight, and opportunityCostUsdt prices the unrecovered leg against the mark. The whole structure is reconstructable from the paper fill stream by runId.
nodes.norm_label: completed cycles, not realized pnl, as the success metric

nodes.label: Close-before-open tick ordering
nodes.rationale: Strict tick order: harvest rebuy, accumulation recovery sell, harvest sell, accumulation buy — obligations close before new ones open, and only ONE action submits per tick. This is not cosmetic: a dip is simultaneously rebuy-eligible AND a fresh sell bucket, so a sell-first ordering sold into the very dip it should have rebought and never reached the rebuy step (the June-10 zero-rebuy bug). The driver additionally refuses to open a sell while ANY rebuy is eligible, reporting SELL_HELD_FOR_REBUY.

nodes.label: Stale paper order cancellation (silent-freeze fix)
nodes.rationale: The one-order-in-flight gate could freeze forever and silently: a paper order that missed its fill probability rests, price moves away from the limit, and it never fills or cancels. Orders older than max(60s, 4 ticks) are cancelled and every waiting tick reports PENDING_ORDER_WAIT so the stall is visible in summaries instead of looking like an idle market.

nodes.label: Zone-gated sells replace avgCost anchoring
nodes.rationale: Sells are gated by market zone rather than by an avgCost floor, which fixes the 'idle below cost' trap where the harvester stopped working entirely whenever price sat under the entry basis. Profit comes from the sell-to-rebuy spread, not from selling above cost. Zone C and above harvest at REDUCED aggression (0.5x size). Price-move backoff clears when price travels more than a bucket width from the rejected price.

nodes.label: Risk params sourced from cfg, not soak settings
nodes.rationale: Only cosmetic knobs live in SoakSettings; RESERVE_FLOOR and all risk-band params come straight from cfg so the soak can never diverge from the RiskEngine that enforces them. The startup Telegram message echoes the params the PROCESS actually received, making laptop/.env/server config drift visible in the first message of every run.
nodes.norm_label: risk params sourced from cfg, not soak settings

nodes.label: Fill routing by order reason (harvest vs accumulation)
nodes.rationale: onPaperFill inspects order.reason: acc-* fills go to the AccumulationEngine's separate cycle tracker, everything else is harvest. Balances and cost basis are shared across both, cycle bookkeeping deliberately is not — the two strategies compete for the same USDT but must be accounted separately. order.price is passed through as intentPrice so bucket occupancy anchors pre-slippage.
nodes.norm_label: fill routing by order reason (harvest vs accumulation)

nodes.label: Conservative zone-view fallback
nodes.rationale: If the zone manager is enabled but has not evaluated yet, the driver receives CONSERVATIVE (rebuy only, REDUCED aggression) rather than an open permission set; if the manager is disabled entirely it receives legacy DEFAULT_ALLOW. The uninitialized case fails closed, the deliberately-off case fails to prior behavior.

nodes.label: Aggregate-and-flush reporting (v2)
nodes.rationale: v1 pushed every fill and produced 1,856 messages, which made the channel unreadable. v2 keeps a rolling window plus a cumulative run counter and flushes only when activity is non-zero; HALT still escapes immediately. Reject REASONS are counted, not just reject totals — bare counts made the Jun-11 failure undiagnosable. Stop emits a final window flush plus a full PAPER_SOAK_RUN_RECORD comparable across soaks.

nodes.label: NAV baseline captured at start
nodes.rationale: Baseline NAV (inventory at mark plus USDT) is snapshotted at startup so every later snapshot can show delta-vs-start alongside the starting mark. This separates 'the strategy made money' from 'the market went up', which realized PnL alone cannot distinguish for a treasury that holds inventory.

nodes.label: Disposable mirror of real treasury accounting
nodes.rationale: The virtual account publishes its fake balances into the StateEngine (source 'paper-soak') specifically so the REAL Risk and Sizing engines evaluate them unmodified, and it derives cost basis through the same pure deriveTreasury() the real treasury uses. Nothing touches the durable ledger or DB — it is fully disposable. The synthetic PAPER-OPENING fill exists only to give the harvester a cost basis to trade against. A synthetic taker fee is charged on every paper fill so paper PnL stays pessimistic.
nodes.norm_label: disposable mirror of real treasury accounting

nodes.label: Bugs encoded as named regression cases
nodes.rationale: Each historical failure has a dedicated named case: 1a slipped-fill stranding, 1c the 255-sells bucket-straddle (with a price deliberately chosen to straddle a 15bps boundary), 3b the June-10 rebuy-starvation, 3c the silent pending-order freeze. The driver is tested through hand-rolled fakes for pipeline/registry/account/reporter/stateEngine, so tick-ordering discipline is verified without any exchange, DB, or timer.
nodes.norm_label: bugs encoded as named regression cases

nodes.label: Truth ownership + single-dispatcher model
nodes.rationale: Three tiers of truth: exchange is ultimate, StateEngine is operational (in-memory, rebuilt on boot), DB is checkpoint. Each action type names exactly which module is allowed to dispatch it, and the union type encodes that permission in the `source` field so a wrong writer is a compile error rather than a runtime mystery. Initial mode is READ_ONLY and recoveryComplete starts false, so execution is gated closed until state recovery fires. ACCOUNT_CLEARED wipes only the in-memory display mirror; the durable treasury ledger is deliberately separate.

nodes.label: Long-poll + sender allowlist control plane
nodes.rationale: getUpdates long-polling avoids a webhook, a public URL, and nginx entirely — the trading box stays headless with no inbound surface. Authorization is fail-closed: only the configured chat id or an explicitly allow-listed user id is honoured, and unauthorized commands are logged and dropped without a reply. Handler exceptions are caught and reported to the user rather than killing the poll loop.

nodes.label: Fire-and-forget notification contract
nodes.rationale: notify() never throws and never blocks: a Telegram outage or a 5s timeout must not stall or fail a trading tick. Missing token/chat id disables the transport silently with one warning instead of erroring at every call site, so Telegram is an observability channel and never a dependency of execution.

nodes.label: Cross-venue fill union
nodes.rationale: The treasury holds ZIG regardless of venue, so inventory, cost basis and harvested PnL are computed over the union of fills from BOTH exchanges rather than per-exchange. State is never mutated in place: ingest dedups by fillId, appends to the durable ledger, and everything else is re-derived, so boot is just load-ledger-and-rebuild. Snapshot writes self-disable permanently on a missing table so a schema gap degrades observability but never trading.

nodes.label: Append-only, never-update ledger invariant
nodes.rationale: Fills are only ever inserted — never updated, never deleted. Dedup rides on the unique fillId so a duplicate insert (P2002) is an expected, idempotent no-op rather than an error, which makes reconciliation replays safe. Fill ids prefixed PAPER- are hard-rejected at the boundary so simulated fills can never contaminate the durable treasury memory. Treasury state is always fully reconstructable by reloading the ledger and re-running deriveTreasury().

nodes.label: Chaos-first, then contiguous price bands
nodes.rationale: CHAOTIC regime or unhealthy exchange/reconciliation wins before any price bucketing, mirroring the volatility classifier's precedence. Below the active band is its own zone specifically so the system does not catch a falling knife, and above it is a breakout candidate. Bands are validated contiguous and ascending in @zig/config so classification has no gaps or overlaps and needs no tie-breaking.
